children.prompt: Explain why this is a prism.

answer.short: It has identical opposite rectangular bases joined by rectangular sides.
answer.worked: Its opposite rectangular bases are identical and are joined by rectangular sides. Every cross-section parallel to a base is identical to that base, so the cross-section is uniform.

children.prompt: Explain why this is not a prism.

answer.short: Its cross-sections parallel to the base change size, so its cross-section is not uniform.
answer.worked: Circular cross-sections parallel to the base become smaller towards the apex, so they are not identical to the base. The cone does not have a uniform cross-section. Its circular base is also not a polygon.

content.prompt: Calculate volume by counting cubes. Each cube is $1\text{ cm}^3$.

spec.description: Four individually divided unit cubes in one layer, with a three-cube diagonal row and a rear-right extension adjoining its middle cube.
spec.mathematics: Occupied unit cells (x,y,z): (0,0,0), (1,0,0), (2,0,0), (1,-1,0). Projection has x down-right, y down-left and z vertical. Opaque faces occlude internal edges; no hidden edges are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Question figure contains cubes only; no count or volume is printed.

spec.description: A single-layer four-by-three rectangle with an interior cube missing and visible shaded inner walls.
spec.mathematics: Occupied cells have x=0,1,2,3; y=0,1,2; z=0, excluding (2,1,0). Projection has x down-right, y down-left and z vertical. Explicit opaque cube faces preserve the opening and occlude internal edges.
spec.answerVisibility: No count, measurements or volume are printed.

answer.worked:
A full layer has $4\times3=12$ cubes. One cube is missing.
$$\begin{align*}V&=(12-1)\times1\\V&=11\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Provisional reconstruction of a low platform with two lateral extensions and one raised cube at the rear centre.
spec.mathematics: Candidate occupied cells: x,y=0,1,2 at z=0, plus (3,0,0), (0,3,0), and (0,0,1). The supporting cell (0,0,0) is partly occluded. This model requires source comparison before acceptance.
spec.answerVisibility: No count or volume is printed. The proposed answer is held separately for review.

answer.worked:
The bottom layer contains $3\times3+2=11$ cubes, with one cube above.
$$\begin{align*}V&=(11+1)\times1\\V&=12\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Cuboid with a four-by-two front grid, four-by-three top grid and three-by-two right grid.
spec.mathematics: Solid occupies [0,4] ���� [0,3] × [0,2]. Viewing projection has horizontal x, depth y up-right and vertical z. Visible faces are y=0, x=4 and z=2. Hidden faces and edges are omitted.
spec.answerVisibility: Only unit divisions are shown; no dimensions or answer labels.

answer.worked:
Each layer contains $4\times3=12$ cubes. There are 2 layers.
$$V=12\times2=24\text{ cm}^3$$

spec.description: Three-step solid with front heights three, two and one, extruded through two depth units.
spec.mathematics: Occupied unit cells have x=0,1,2; y=0,1; and 0≤z<3−x. Visible surfaces comprise front unit squares, top treads and exposed right-facing risers. Depth projects up-right.
spec.answerVisibility: No dimensions, cube counts or answers appear on the figure.

answer.worked:
The layers contain 6, 4 and 2 cubes.
$$V=6+4+2=12\text{ cm}^3$$

spec.description: L-shaped solid with front column heights six, six, six, three and three, extruded three cubes deep.
spec.mathematics: Occupied cells have y=0,1,2; x=0,1,2 with 0≤z<6, or x=3,4 with 0≤z<3. Visible surfaces are the front, both top levels, the upper step wall and outer right wall. Depth projects up-right.
spec.answerVisibility: Unit divisions are visible; no dimensions or answers are printed.

answer.worked:
Each of the bottom 3 layers contains $5\times3=15$ cubes. Each of the upper 3 layers contains $3\times3=9$ cubes.
$$\begin{align*}V&=3\times15+3\times9\\V&=45+27\\V&=72\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 15, branching A4 rolling illustration at lower left
spec.description: Landscape A4 sheet, 297 mm across and 210 mm high. A right arrow leads to an upright rolled cylinder captioned Curl up the long side; a downward arrow leads to a horizontal rolled cylinder captioned Curl up the short side.
spec.mathematics: Sheet side ratio 297:210. Long-side rolling gives circumference 297 mm and height 210 mm; short-side rolling gives circumference 210 mm and height 297 mm. Narrow longitudinal openings illustrate the rolling operation and do not specify a measured gap. Upright rolled surface uses cylindrical angular domain -80 to 260 degrees, omitting the front sector from 260 to 280 degrees. Horizontal surface is viewed from the positive axial direction; its front slit uses the same angular omission. Both are open rolled surfaces, not closed solids with filled end disks.
spec.answerVisibility: Sheet dimensions and source outcome captions only. Circumferences, radii, volumes and comparison are answer content.

answer.short: The cylinder labelled “Curl up the long side” has the greater volume.
answer.worked:
Curl up the short side:
$$\begin{align*}C&=2\pi r\\210&=2\pi r\\r&=\frac{210}{2\pi}\,\mathrm{mm}\\V_{\text{curl short side}}&=\pi r^2h\\V_{\text{curl short side}}&=\pi\left(\frac{210}{2\pi}\right)^2(297)\\V_{\text{curl short side}}&=\frac{13\,097\,700}{4\pi}\,\mathrm{mm}^3\end{align*}$$
Curl up the long side:
$$\begin{align*}C&=2\pi r\\297&=2\pi r\\r&=\frac{297}{2\pi}\,\mathrm{mm}\\V_{\text{curl long side}}&=\pi r^2h\\V_{\text{curl long side}}&=\pi\left(\frac{297}{2\pi}\right)^2(210)\\V_{\text{curl long side}}&=\frac{18\,523\,890}{4\pi}\,\mathrm{mm}^3\end{align*}$$
Since $18\,523\,890>13\,097\,700$, $\therefore$ the cylinder curled up the long side has the larger volume.
